claims.statement: Production's Control-Tower support services are three separate Komodo ResourceSync stacks — prod-audit (the OpenSearch audit sink), prod-observability (LangFuse + otel-lgtm + OPA + Unleash) and prod-vault (deliberately dormant) — each declared as its own [[stack]] block with deploy = true, so each is independently up/down-able; prod-audit is a root with no `after`, prod-observability's edge is ordering only, and prod-vault hangs off prod-auth because it is logically in the auth tier.

A deployed support stack does not by itself change application behavior: the consumer composes reference every Control-Tower variable as plain ${VAR}, never ${VAR:?}, and each capability is gated in the consumer's own source (audit_sink on OPENSEARCH_URL, observability on LANGFUSE_*/OTEL_*, opa on OPA_URL, flags on UNLEASH_URL), so unset means a silent no-op. Rollback is therefore removing the consumer env and/or deleting the support [[stack]] block, with no app redeploy needed to disable a capability.

The support composes are fail-fast (every credential is ${VAR:?}) while the consumer composes are not, so an unseeded Komodo Variable aborts a support deploy by design but can never abort the app; fifteen new masked Variables are needed (13 observability + 2 audit), the dormant Vault needs none, and TAILNET_HOST is reused from prod-auth for LangFuse's tailnet NEXTAUTH_URL. The object store's Variable is LANGFUSE_RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY. The retired LANGFUSE_MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD was deliberately retained in Komodo through the RustFS cutover's rollback window — a revert restores the line that needs it, and a revert cannot recreate a Komodo Variable — and was then deleted together with the old volume and the registry package on 2026-10-24, when the operator closed that window early (item #826); nothing in the tree reads it any more.

Control-Tower consumer wiring is least-privilege rather than symmetric: prod-mcm-bff consumes only the audit sink and OPA (OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD plus the literal OPA_URL), while the gateway on prod-movie-assistant is the primary emitter and additionally receives the LangFuse keys and the Unleash CLIENT token (never the admin token).

The audit sink is isolated on its own external agent-audit-network, joined only by agent-audit-opensearch, its init container and the gateway/BFF consumers, so keycloak and mc-service cannot reach it; adding that network to APPROVED_NETWORKS and the `vault` volume prefix to VOLUME_RE was the entire guardrail delta for the feature.

Komodo counts any exited container as unhealthy, so every one-shot init container in this stack set must provision and then idle (`… && exec sleep infinity`) behind a trivial passing healthcheck; where a downstream service needs the init's result the dependency gates on a completion marker instead — langfuse-rustfs-init creates the bucket then touches /tmp/ready, its healthcheck tests for that marker, and langfuse-worker depends on service_healthy because a never-exiting container can never satisfy service_completed_successfully. The prod stay-alive shape versus the dev true one-shot is asserted by a guard test rather than left to memory.

Non-root image runtimes and bind-mount ownership are the dominant class of prod-only failures here: every symptom passed local `docker compose config` and only surfaced on the prod host, including the OpenSearch memlock rlimit EPERM, the uid-1000 init container unable to mkdir a root-owned bind mount, Vault's permission-denied raft path and `Failed to lock memory`, and Vault's double-loaded listener config causing `bind: address already in use` — so diagnosis belongs in container logs on the prod host, not in the compose file.

The working Vault configuration needs all four of /vault/file (a vault-owned image dir, so an empty volume inherits vault:vault and no chown is needed), disable_mlock = true, cap_add: IPC_LOCK and command: ["server"] together, and each rationale is stated in place: vault.hcl carries the mount path (because /vault/data is absent from the image and would land root-owned, so vault uid 100 could not create vault.db) and disable_mlock (the prod daemon's memlock rlimit is finite, so mlockall fails even with the cap, and raft/BoltDB mmaps are the recommended case for it), while the vault compose carries the cap and the bare `server` command (the entrypoint already appends -config=/vault/config, so passing the file explicitly loads the listener twice and the second instance dies with `bind: address already in use`). The cap's original second reason — without it the entrypoint took a fallback path that double-started vault — no longer applies to the shipped hashicorp/vault:2.2 image (spec 081 US8c), whose changelog drops the build-time cap_ipc_lock, but the cap is kept deliberately: it is harmless and the line matters again if the image is ever rolled back to 1.x. The page repeats the rationale in its prod-only gotchas table.

prod-vault is deployed uninitialized and sealed on purpose, and its healthcheck overrides ?uninitcode=200&sealedcode=200&standbycode=200 so that dormant state reads as healthy to Komodo; running `vault operator init`/unseal is explicitly out of scope for this rollout, and the overridden codes resume their real meaning once an operator does init and unseal.

The only tailnet-reachable operator UIs in this stack set are langfuse-web and the Grafana UI inside otel-lgtm, both published as plain 0.0.0.0 HOST:CONTAINER binds in the prod-reserved 19000–19099 range and kept tailnet-only by the host firewall; the OTLP ports stay unpublished because the gateway reaches otel-lgtm by internal DNS, and the broad bind (rather than a tailnet-IP prefix) exists because the rootless daemon starts before tailscaled at boot — the boot race documented in the prod-reboot-resilience runbook, with the range's collision gate in scripts/check-prod-ci-port-collision.mjs.

The audit writer account is provisioned and self-verified at runtime by the agent-audit-init service rather than by a stored credential: init-audit-user.sh PUT-upserts a write-only `agent-audit` role (create_index plus write/index and write/bulk on mcm-agent-audit and mcm-agent-audit-*), the user and the role mapping, then asserts write 201 and read/search/delete 403 against a document that demonstrably exists — a missing doc would answer 404 either way, so a mere "not 200" check would pass vacuously on a wrongly-permissive role.

The Langfuse 4 + ClickHouse 25 cutover recreates the Postgres, ClickHouse-data and ClickHouse-logs volumes and discards production Langfuse trace history (ratified by ADR-0002 §4), and the volume work must precede the merge because Komodo reconciles prod-observability from main. Because the volumes are external: true, compose never removes them, and because a stopped container still holds its mounts, `docker volume rm` fails with `volume is in use` until the holding containers are removed — measured on the 2026-09-13 cutover.

The Langfuse cutover's rollback is a revert-and-redeploy that does not restore the discarded traces — Langfuse 3 re-initialises the now-empty volumes — and the object-store volume is deliberately not recreated by this cutover because it holds blobs rather than schema and its own replacement is the separate RustFS migration. The cutover is a contained planned outage: no non-Langfuse service in the stack depends_on langfuse, and the gateway's tracing is fire-and-forget, so turns are unaffected.

ADR-0002 §4's ratification that a cutover may discard the trace store is scoped to that cutover and does not make later ClickHouse majors data-free: a ClickHouse major for the production Langfuse stack arrived through a routine Renovate image update over live production traces, and the end-to-end CI job never starts the observability stack, so a green CI said nothing about it — which is why stateful datastore majors now require an explicit dependency-dashboard tick.

The OpenSearch 2 → 3 audit-sink upgrade preserves history by snapshot and restore, which forces two deploys in a non-negotiable order because path.repo is a static setting: Deploy A adds the snapshot volume and path.repo while still on 2.x, restarts, registers the repository and snapshots; Deploy B starts 3.x on a NEW empty data volume, re-registers the repository (cluster state does not survive a new cluster) and restores. One deploy cannot work — it would mean snapshotting before the repository exists or replacing the data volume before the snapshot is taken.

Because 3.x starts on a new volume and the 2.x data volume is never touched, two independent copies of the audit history exist throughout the OpenSearch upgrade and its rollback is non-lossy — reverting Deploy B's compose to the 2.x digest and the ORIGINAL data volume restores the previous state, with the snapshot as a second way back. Deleting the old volume or the snapshot is a separate deliberate act and is not part of the procedure.

The OpenSearch upgrade's acceptance check is an exact document count rather than a health check: 5,276 documents in mcm-agent-audit was a reading taken before the decision, not a constant, so the live count must be re-measured during Deploy A and reproduced exactly after the restore, with the check taken before the init container is restarted because that container adds one more init-verify doc.

An empty result from a filtered query means "no match", not "no data": the audit history was nearly missed because `_cat/indices/mcm-agent-audit-*` returned empty (the pattern needs no trailing wildcard and the real index name is mcm-agent-audit), and that empty result came one step from justifying the destruction of a security audit trail. The snapshot scope is therefore mcm-agent-audit only, with include_global_state false, because restoring system indices such as .opendistro_security across a major is a conflict risk with no upside.

During the OpenSearch upgrade the agent-audit-init container must be stopped before the restore, because init-audit-user.sh POSTs a verification document on startup and the writer role carries create_index, so on the empty 3.x volume the stack re-creates mcm-agent-audit first and the restore fails with `cannot restore index [mcm-agent-audit] because an open index with same name already exists in the cluster` — measured on the 2026-09-13 cutover. The recovery, if it happens anyway, is safe only while docs.count is ~1 (the init-verify doc); anything else means another writer and a stop.

ClickHouse in prod-observability is bounded in two independent ways: a container mem_limit of 4g with a matching memswap_limit and a CPU ceiling, so it cannot starve the shared host (measured at ~725% CPU with swap full on 2026-10-02, slowing every CI job 2-3x), and a mounted mcm-system-logs.xml that removes trace_log and text_log and puts a 3-day TTL on the other existing system-log tables, because with image defaults those diagnostic tables grew to 128 GiB and 28 GiB against 84 KiB of actual Langfuse data. Only tables that already exist may be declared, since declaring a *_log section enables that table; one table is exempt because its default section defines a full <engine> — adding a separate <ttl> to opentelemetry_span_log makes ClickHouse refuse to start (measured on the 25.12 image), so it is left at its default.

The prod-only failure table's two smaller traps are still load-bearing: the audit-init container must use an image shipping both bash and curl (init-audit-user.sh is #!/usr/bin/env bash, so curlimages/curl cannot run it) and its entrypoint pre-creates the sibling stacks dir the script cd's into before its guard, or set -euo pipefail aborts everything; and the BFF's audit POST needs OPENSEARCH_INSECURE_TLS=true because OpenSearch serves a self-signed cert and the sink sets rejectUnauthorized:false only when that flag is truthy, while the gateway's httpx sink needs no flag.

The OPA healthcheck is driven through the opa binary rather than a shell utility, because the -debug variant's busybox ships no wget, curl or nc — the previous wget check failed on every run, leaving OPA marked unhealthy from ~2026-09-10 with a FailingStreak of 130,247 by 2026-10-03 while it served fine; the -debug variant itself is still required because the distroless image has no shell at all.

Enabling prod-observability followed a capacity check on the shared prod host rather than an assumption of headroom: ~48 GiB RAM was available against ~2.2 GiB of actual container RSS, and observability (~6-7 GiB) plus the audit sink (~1.5 GiB) left ~40 GiB free, so the decision was always-on with no opt-in fallback and ClickHouse's mem_limit retained; the check is to be re-run before any future footprint increase.

The OpenSearch snapshot repository lives in its own external volume (agent-audit-opensearch-snapshots) rather than inside the data volume, because the 2→3 upgrade replaces the data volume and a repository inside it would be destroyed at the exact moment it is the only copy. The resource-naming gate admits this with a narrowly scoped agent-<...>-snapshots form (VOLUME_SNAPSHOTS_RE) instead of the volume being misnamed as -data.

init-audit-user.sh no longer echoes the credentials it provisions. It used to print both passwords in full, and once agent-audit-init began running it in production that output went to container stdout, leaving both live credentials in docker logs agent-audit-init, in Komodo's log view and in anything shipping those logs — a direct violation of the stack's never-log list. It now prints where the credentials live (dev: the gitignored stacks/audit.env; prod: Komodo Variables), never what they are.

The prod Langfuse event/media object store is no longer built in-repo: feature 080 replaced every instance with the digest-pinned upstream rustfs/rustfs image, which runs as its own uid (10001) with no compose `user:` key — a fresh named volume inherits the image's /data with that ownership and any other uid fails at startup. All shipped instances (the dev and prod observability composes and the backups compose) pin the same 1.0.4 line on one shared index digest, and the bucket-init one-shot langfuse-rustfs-init reuses that same pinned image; the object-store guard test holds the whole shape (digest-pinned tag, no `user:` key, RUSTFS_* credentials, the readiness probe, the prod stay-alive init, and that all three files pin one identical image), so a split between the server and its init cannot arise from a hand edit and the digest itself is left to the compose files and Renovate.

The RustFS cutover moves production's data in place: the old drive is copied to a new external volume that RustFS reads while the original is never written, so rollback is a revert onto the untouched old volume and the old store is deleted only after the 14-day rollback window closes. Merging the PR IS the deploy, so the copy must exist first — the new compose mounts an external volume only the migration tool's `copy --apply` creates, and a deploy before that aborts with `external volume "observability-langfuse-rustfs-data" not found`, creates zero containers and does not create the volume, leaving previously deployed containers running and unchanged (measured 2026-10-11).

The object-store migration tool ran ON the prod host from a repository checkout through scripts/object-store-migration.sh, because the host has no `node`: the wrapper copied the Docker CLI out of a digest-pinned image, ran the tool in a digest-pinned node container with the host's rootless socket mounted, copied the evidence directory in and back out, and passed S3 credentials by NAME from the shell environment rather than on a command line. This is now the record of a completed cutover rather than a procedure — the tool and its wrapper were deleted by spec 080 T048 (2026-11-01), so the commands the runbook's history blocks name no longer exist.

The migration tool refused rather than guessed at every step: `copy` without `--apply` was refused (there was no dry-run spelling — `inventory` was how you looked) and the wrapper refused it before any container existed, as it did `rehearse`; the tool also refused an existing target volume, a source still mounted by a running container, a volume that did not exist (it was never created by looking at it), and an inventory whose search instrument failed its self-test, because a BusyBox grep in its default locale misses markers inside a binary xl.meta so a zero proved nothing until the search had been shown to find a planted marker. A drive classified as migratable only if its format was xl-single with exactly one set and one drive and there were zero SSE and zero tiered objects.

The cutover's own acceptance records were asserted, not just produced: copy.json had to show targetPreexisted false, entriesNotOwnedByRuntimeUid 0 and equal source digests before and after — a source that changed during the copy was no longer a valid rollback target and the tool said so instead of continuing — and `verify` compared the running new store against the pre-migration manifest and exited non-zero on any discrepancy.

A guard test (scripts/__tests__/no-minio-references.guard.test.mjs) scans every git-tracked file's path and content case-insensitively for the retired object store's name against a closed exemption list, and proves it read the tree rather than a handful of files (a floor of ~1,800 scanned text files). The exemptions are of three kinds — path exemptions for places where the name is legitimately history (specs/**, docs/decisions/**, docs/proposals/**, the generated openwiki/**, pnpm-lock.yaml and the guard itself), line exemptions for live files that must name the literal (the secret scanner's detection set, the dev-env generator's pre-080 migration, the naming gate's RETIRED_KEYS line and the object-store guard's prohibition on the retired MINIO_* aliases), and token exemptions that strip citations of the fixed spec-directory and guard/contract names. Every entry must match at least one real file or line or it fails as stale, exactly as an unmatched allowlist entry does; anything else — a runbook case study included — must be wrapped in a `<!-- history:begin -->` … `<!-- history:end -->` block, honoured only under docs/runbooks/**, and the exemptions that named the migration tool were removed with the tool.

`restart: always` on every long-running prod service is a self-enforcing property rather than a convention: scripts/check-prod-restart-policy.mjs scans every infrastructure-as-code/docker/**/compose.prod.yaml and fails on a missing restart policy, on `unless-stopped`, and on `no`/`on-failure` for anything that is not a genuine one-shot (name matching -init/-seed/-rs-init or createbucket), so a new prod service added with the obvious-looking default goes red in the gate instead of dark after a reboot.

Six of the one-time stateful cutovers on the production support stacks now stand on record. Three of them — the feature-080 RustFS object-store swap, the feature-071 OpenSearch 2→3 upgrade, and the spec-081 US8b Postgres 16→18 move — put the new state on a NEW external volume and leave the previous volume untouched as the rollback, so their rollback is a revert-and-redeploy rather than a data restore. The Langfuse 4 + ClickHouse 25 cutover (feature 072) recreated its volumes in place and deliberately discarded the production trace store, a trade ratified by ADR-0002 §4 at that cutover only. The remaining two are the schema-carrying Langfuse minors — 4.56.0 → 4.68.0 (spec 081 US8 PR 8d, item 839) and 4.68.0 → 4.72.0 (item 895) — which migrate both stores in place, so there the pre-merge backup is what turns a rollback into a restore instead of a loss.

Postgres 18 will not start on a pre-18 data directory: measured 2026-10-20 on a copy of a real 16 Unleash volume it exits 1 with the old volume mounted at the 18 parent /var/lib/postgresql and again at the pre-18 /var/lib/postgresql/data, and it also exits 1 on an EMPTY volume mounted at /data while leaving an anonymous volume behind. With `restart: always` that is a crash loop for both observability databases the moment the merge deploys, so the compose mounts the PARENT /var/lib/postgresql (18 keeps its cluster under /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker) on new external volumes observability-{langfuse,unleash}-postgres-v18-data, leaving the 16 volumes untouched as the rollback — the same -v3-data shape feature 071 used for OpenSearch.

For the spec-081 US8b cutover a merge to main IS the deploy, so the timing of the -v18-data volumes is the whole risk: merging before the volumes exist is safe because the deploy fails up front with `external volume "…-v18-data" not found` and the 16 containers keep running unchanged, whereas merging after creating the volumes but before the Unleash dump/restore is the outcome to avoid because Unleash comes up healthy on an EMPTY database, unleash-seed recreates only its three default-off flags, every other flag, strategy and API token is gone, and nothing reports it. The same mechanism leaves a developer's local 18 stack on an empty volume, where unleash-seed likewise recreates only the three default-off flags.

The US8b data decision is asymmetric: Unleash flag state is preserved by pg_dumpall from the 16 instance and a restore onto 18 in a throwaway container before the merge, verified by a pre/post table-count diff over features, feature_strategies, api_tokens, feature_environments-where-enabled and migrations that must print COUNTS-EQUAL (the restore's stderr being exactly the two 'already exists' lines) and, after the deploy, LIVE-COUNTS-EQUAL against the same 16 baseline; while Langfuse's Postgres is deliberately discarded per ADR-0002 §4 and re-initialised by LANGFUSE_INIT_*, which recreates the mcm org, the movie-assistant project and its keys so gateway tracing keeps working, at the cost of anything created by hand in the Langfuse UI. ClickHouse and RustFS are not touched by this cutover, and only the three writers (unleash-service, langfuse-web, langfuse-worker) are stopped for the dump window.

langfuse-postgres and unleash-postgres reference one identical pinned Postgres image, which is why they can only move together, and that is enforced rather than remembered: scripts/__tests__/langfuse-postgres-shared-pin.guard.test.mjs asserts against both the dev and the prod observability compose one identical digest for both services, on the 18 line, mounting /var/lib/postgresql and never the pre-18 /var/lib/postgresql/data, on a volume that is not the one holding the 16 data and whose name carries the -v18 marker. The spec-081 change also discharged the observability-only `allowedVersions: "<17"` hard hold in favour of renovate.json's stateful-datastore major approval tick — and the current reading of that successor is the rule plus renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs, NOT docs/runbooks/renovate.md, whose "database MAJOR waits in Pending Approval" paragraph still describes the observability postgres as held below 17 outright and therefore never reaching the approval list.

The US8b rollback is non-lossy for Unleash — reverting the merge puts the compose back on postgres:16-alpine and the ORIGINAL observability-{langfuse,unleash}-postgres-data volumes, which hold the state exactly as it was when the writers were stopped — but flag changes made on 18 after the cutover are not carried back, and the pg_dumpall of the 16 instance is a second way back; because main is protected that revert is itself a pull request (git revert -m 1 <merge-sha>) which must merge before the prod-observability redeploy. Until the merge lands the window can be abandoned losslessly, since the 16 databases keep running throughout and only the three writers are stopped. The pre-seed wait must use pg_isready over TCP rather than the socket, because a socket-only check can pass against the entrypoint's temporary init server, and containers must be addressed by name because a hand-run docker compose cannot work against a Komodo-managed stack.

The spec-081 US8b observability Postgres 16→18 cutover is no longer merely rehearsed: it ran in production on 2026-10-20 (PR #809, commit 44817a42), with Unleash's table counts identical at all three readings — the 16 instance, the pre-seeded 18 volume and the live 18 database (api_tokens 2, env_enabled 0, feature_strategies 1, features 3, migrations 397) — both databases running 18.6 on the observability-{langfuse,unleash}-postgres-v18-data volumes and Langfuse fresh and healthy on its re-initialised database, while the step list itself had been built on a dev-container rehearsal earlier the same day that also verified the rollback to the untouched 16 volume.

Three faults in the first version of the US8b steps are why the shipped commands are shaped as they are: pg_dumpall ends with the completion marker, then '--', then a blank line, so tail -2 never shows the marker and the check greps for it instead; a read -rs inside a pasted block consumes the next pasted line as its input and the bare `-e POSTGRES_PASSWORD` form passed nothing through this host's docker CLI, so the password is read from the RUNNING 16 container with printenv and passed explicitly (otherwise the 18 entrypoint exits with `Database is uninitialized and superuser password is not specified`); and the pre-seed wait loop otherwise spun forever on an already-exited container (`cannot exec in a stopped container`, once every 2 s), so it is now bounded, detects the exit and prints the logs, with the docker rm moved to a later block so a failed start leaves its logs readable.

A Langfuse minor can still carry schema: 4.57–4.68 add 11 Postgres (Prisma) migrations and ClickHouse migrations 52–53 (audit-log staging and relay, among others), and the web container applies them on its first start, so for the 4.56.0 → 4.68.0 cutover the merge IS the migration. Per ADR-0002 §4 the trace store need not survive, but a backup taken first turns a rollback into a restore instead of a loss; the pre-merge backup is a pg_dumpall of langfuse-postgres plus a cold tar of the stopped ClickHouse data volume, and the acceptance reading afterwards is _prisma_migrations at 460 with ClickHouse migration 53 applied, zero error lines in either container and a new trace readable.

For the Langfuse 4.56.0 → 4.68.0 cutover a digest revert ALONE does not roll back: measured 2026-10-25, 4.56.0 started on a store that 4.68.0 had migrated crash-loops with `error: no migration found for version 53` (ClickHouse), because the older image cannot run on the newer schema. A rollback therefore restores both stores (or recreates them empty) BEFORE the reverted digest starts, and because main is protected the revert itself goes through a pull request.

Two smaller traps shape the Langfuse 4.68 minor's checks: `wget localhost:3000` inside langfuse-web exits 4 because the server binds to the container hostname, so the health checks must target `$HOSTNAME` (and the worker's equivalent is on its own port); and neither langfuse-web nor langfuse-worker declares a compose healthcheck, so `docker ps` shows `Up`, never `healthy`, and health must be read from the HTTP endpoint and the logs instead.

The Langfuse 4.56.0 → 4.68.0 minor completed in production on 2026-10-25 (PR #852 merged pinned to ef2f199f as 89bd8acd) and closed PR 8d. Unlike the app stacks there was no cd-deploy promote commit: the Komodo sync deployed prod-observability directly, because this change builds no image. The operator pre-merge backup ran at ~01:04 UTC (ClickHouse 319M and Postgres `15 MB|449` read before, pg_dumpall marker found at 0.9 MB, ClickHouse cold copy tar exit=0 / CH-HEALTHY / GZIP-OK at 138 MB, WEB-OK on 4.56.0) and is kept on the host at ~/839-langfuse-468. Post-deploy both containers ran 4.68.0 Up with health {"status":"OK","version":"4.68.0"} and {"status":"ok"}, _prisma_migrations read 460, ClickHouse migrations 52/u create_audit_logs and 53/u add_skill_observation_references were applied, web and worker logged zero error lines, and a trace landed via the worker's ClickhouseWriter — the same acceptance reading the runbook prescribes.

The 4.68.0 bump's allowlist work was mixed rather than uniform, and the page's "re-key at the cause" rule is the shape while this is the instance: the two `next` advisories the new version discharged were DELETED, while the three that still block on the exact 4.68.0 digests — the base-image ca-certificates CVE on web and worker, and the bundled @sentry/nextjs CVE on web — were RE-KEYED 4\.56\.0 → 4\.68\.0 with their 2026-11-20 expiry unchanged, so the gate passed with 0 unmatched entries and --check-expiring still opens its warning window on 2026-11-06. renovate.json needed no edit at all, because the `langfuse` packageRule and the stateful-major dependencyDashboardApproval rule match by package name with no version in them — recorded as a fact rather than changed cosmetically. Those three re-keyed entries were themselves discharged a week later, when the 4.72.0 bump landed on clean rebuilds (see the item-895 claim).

The 4.68.0 upgrade path was measured on the dev stack rather than inferred from a fresh start: the stack was first brought up on 4.56.0 and an agent turn traced, then web and worker alone were moved to 4.68.0 on the SAME volumes, which is how the migration path itself got verified. Prisma applied 11 migrations (460 total, including add_audit_log_staging and its failure columns), ClickHouse applied 52 create_audit_logs and 53 add_skill_observation_references with schema_migrations 53 / dirty 0, both containers logged zero error/warn lines, and both the pre-move and post-move traces sit in ClickHouse events_core — written by the worker's ClickhouseWriter — with October history still readable.

`scripts/__tests__/langfuse-postgres-shared-pin.guard.test.mjs` is four assertions against both the dev and prod observability composes, one per failure shape of the shared Langfuse/Unleash Postgres pin: the two services reference one identical image (with an explicit non-vacuity check that each service still has an image at all), that shared pin is digest-pinned on the 18 line, both services mount the parent `/var/lib/postgresql` and not the pre-18 `/var/lib/postgresql/data`, and both mount a volume that is not the pre-18 one and whose name ends in `-v18-data`. Its comments record that the premise the second test originally protected — "the shared pin stays on 16, because moving it migrates Unleash as a side effect" — was updated at its cause by spec 081 US8b rather than deleted, so the test now reds a regression to 16 or an unreviewed move to 19 instead of a move off 16.

The Renovate side of the US8b hold discharge is asserted as its successor rather than as an absence, because a deliberately discharged hold and a deleted one are indistinguishable once `allowedVersions` is gone: `scripts/__tests__/renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs` checks per observability compose file that no update track (patch, minor, major) carries a version ceiling — a `<17` left behind would block the 18 actually deployed — that a Postgres major on the shared pin requires `dependencyDashboardApproval`, and that the patch track requires no approval so the security patch stream stays automatic, plus a control asserting the observability postgres resolves identically to `keycloak`'s postgres so a surviving file-scoped rule reddens the gate.

The sixth one-time stateful cutover is the Langfuse 4.68.0 → 4.72.0 minor (item 895), the same shape as the 4.68 minor applied to the next version: the merge IS the migration, the pre-merge backup is what turns a rollback into a restore, and a digest revert ALONE would not roll back because 4.68.0 cannot run on a store carrying three Prisma migrations it has never seen. Measured 2026-11-01 on copies of the dev observability volumes: 4.72.0 adds 3 Prisma migrations so `_prisma_migrations` goes 460 → 463, ClickHouse adds no migrations so `schema_migrations` stays at 53, and the backup restores into 4.68.0 (which comes up healthy with a pre-upgrade trace present and a post-upgrade trace absent). It also differs from the 4.68 minor in backing up the object store, because the langfuse-rustfs volume holds the raw OTLP ingestion objects.

Langfuse 4 traces live in ClickHouse's v4 events model: with `LANGFUSE_MIGRATION_V4_WRITE_MODE=events_only`, `GET /api/public/traces/{id}` reads the legacy `traces` table, which is no longer written, so the trace-landed check for the 4.72.0 cutover counts rows in `events_full` instead of using that endpoint; the legacy `trace-create` ingestion event is refused with 400 and traces arrive over `POST /api/public/otel/v1/traces`. `LANGFUSE_MIGRATION_V4_WRITE_MODE=dual` must not be used as a fix — it restores INGESTION only and would mask an unmigrated read path rather than repair it, which is why a guard test polices removed v4 read APIs in source rather than the ingestion side.

The 4.68.0 → 4.72.0 bump discharged the three allowlist entries that had been re-keyed to 4\.68\.0 a week earlier rather than re-keying them again: both langfuse refs moved to 4.72.0 (web sha256:c311fd9db4b6…, worker sha256:aa1724b989a0…), which Trivy 0.76.1 with the gate's criteria reports at zero fixable Criticals on each, so CVE-2026-114406 (ca-certificates, web + worker) and CVE-2026-114139 (@sentry/nextjs, web) were deleted — a re-keyed entry would match nothing and fail guard (063) / --check-expiring under UNMATCHED ENTRIES, and deleting is the direction that restores blocking if either advisory returns.

One paragraph of docs/runbooks/renovate.md still trails the spec-081 US8b discharge: its "A database MAJOR waits in Pending Approval" section describes the observability postgres as held below 17 outright and therefore never reaching the approval list, which was true only before US8b moved the shared Langfuse/Unleash pin to 18 and lifted the ceiling. The current reading lives in renovate.json's stateful-datastore rule (postgres among the database images that require dependencyDashboardApproval on a major) and in renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs, not in that runbook line — so the page flags the trailing sentence rather than relying on it.

The feature-080 RustFS object-store cutover is complete and closed out: production moved to RustFS on 2026-10-16, the cleanup ran early on 2026-10-24 (item #826) deleting the old volume, the Komodo Variable LANGFUSE_MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD and the jumbleknot/minio registry package, and the migration tool, its wrapper and its tests were deleted by spec 080 T048 (2026-11-01), with the guard's temporary exemptions removed and the runbook's live cutover text wrapped in history blocks. The section survives only as the shape of the cutover and the traps it was built around, and the runbook's commands are explicitly not to be looked for.

The fail-fast coupling between a support compose's `${VAR:?}` and its Komodo stack declaration is enforced by a guard rather than remembered: `scripts/__tests__/komodo-stack-env.guard.test.mjs` parses every `[[stack]]` block of `infrastructure-as-code/komodo/stacks.toml` (its `environment` block plus any committed `additional_env_files`) and fails when a variable a prod compose requires with `${VAR:?…}` is supplied by neither — so adding a required variable to a support compose is mechanically a change to that stack's required inputs in stacks.toml. It exists because that coupling broke once: feature 069 repointed the object store's image at the repository's own registry, making prod-observability the fourth consumer of REGISTRY_HOST while stacks.toml declared it for only three, and the deploy failed on `required variable REGISTRY_HOST is missing a value` — invisible to CI because the compose was valid and the dev stack is supplied by the dev env file. Feature 080 removed REGISTRY_HOST from that stack and added LANGFUSE_RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY, the same coupling in the other direction, and the guard went red until the block declared it. The guard is scoped to the `${VAR:?…}` form only (an optional `${VAR}` is by definition allowed to be absent, and comments are stripped so a documented example is not counted), and its instrument check deletes that one stacks.toml line and asserts the gap appears, so it cannot pass by parsing nothing.

The guard that polices removed Langfuse v4 read APIs carries a second, independent test so its first one cannot be satisfied by deletion rather than migration: it asserts `agents/movie-assistant/tests/integration/test_observability_sc008.py` still mentions `cost_usd` and `latency_ms` and still calls `observations.get_many`. That matters because the SC-008 test is credential-gated and SKIPS on a machine without a priced provider, so a dead read path would not have failed loudly — the guarantee would simply have stopped being checked while reading as green. The guard deliberately does not police the ingestion side, because doing so would invite the `LANGFUSE_MIGRATION_V4_WRITE_MODE=dual` "fix", which restores ingestion only and would mask an unmigrated read path.

renovate.json's stateful-datastore rule is what carries the discharged Postgres hold: it puts `postgres` in one `matchPackageNames` list beside `mongodb/mongodb-community-server`, `redis` and `clickhouse/clickhouse-server`, gated by `dependencyDashboardApproval` on `matchUpdateTypes: ["major"]` only, so every database major in the tree waits for an explicit dashboard tick while patches, minors and digest refreshes stay automatic. Its own description records the discharge rather than hiding it — the observability postgres (the shared Langfuse/Unleash pin) was HARD-held below 17 until spec 081 US8b moved both databases to 18 together, and it now rides the tick like every other postgres (keycloak, agent-db) — which is why the ceiling's absence is a successor rather than a hole.

Beyond the shared digest, the prod RustFS instance's security-relevant shape is guard-enforced clause by clause: the console is disabled with RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ENABLE "false" (RustFS's console defaults to ON with CORS `*`, and false closes :9001) and no instance may publish a console port, RUSTFS_OBS_LOG_DIRECTORY is set to the empty string so logs go to stdout rather than the image's default log file that `docker logs` never sees, and the bucket-init one-shot feeds its secret to curl as a config on stdin referenced as `$$S3_SECRET_KEY` — never interpolated into argv, where `docker inspect` and `ps` could read it — alongside the fail-fast `${LANGFUSE_RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY:?…}` environment reference and a `service_healthy` dependency on the server, so none of those shortcuts can arrive as a hand edit.
